text: Staging models only rename and cast. The real logic — joins, aggregation, lifetime value — lives one layer up, in the intermediate and mart models this lesson builds.
Three layers, three jobs: staging is a 1:1 rename on one raw source, intermediate is reusable aggregation not meant for direct BI use, and a mart is the finished, business-facing model.

int_orders__payment_summary aggregates every payment per order, computing a total amount paid and a payment count. More than one downstream mart needs this, which is exactly why it's pulled out as its own reusable intermediate model.

The customers mart builds on ref of orders, not on the staging model directly — a mart referencing another mart, reusing the payment aggregation orders.sql already resolved, instead of redoing that work.
customers and orders are exactly the two models Power BI connects to in Chapter 7, once they pass every test and CI check. Next: adding a snapshot to track customer status as it changes over time.
